title: Ireland unveils blueprint to electrify economy by 2050
excerpt: Dublin's plan takes into account a surge in electricity demand over the coming decades, driven by electric vehicles, industry and rapidly expanding data centres, which will place growing pressure on the national grid.
content_html:
Ireland has announced a sweeping review of its electricity system, with the government promising a blueprint to reshape the country's power sector by 2050 as it races to meet climate targets and electrify its economy.

Irish Climate, Energy and Environment Minister Darragh O'Brien said on Wednesday that work is underway on a long-term strategy to set out how Ireland plans to generate, transmit and regulate electricity through to 2050.

The move from Dublin comes as Ireland has taken the helm of the rotating EU Council Presidency and vowed to make electrification a priority.

The disruption in the Middle East has also revealed how the EU's dependence on imported fossil fuels is leading to higher energy bills and inflation, with roughly an extra €50 billion spent on fossil fuel imports in just 111 days during disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz.

"Ireland's energy transition represents a momentous opportunity for us all, to help make our economy and industries more efficient and competitive, to open new opportunities for businesses, and create tangible benefits for our communities across Ireland," O'Brien said.

The new "Power Sector White Paper" is expected to become the cornerstone of future energy policy, guiding legislation, investment decisions and grid development as Ireland shifts away from fossil fuels towards an electricity-based economy.

The review comes as electricity demand is forecast to surge over the coming decades, driven by electric vehicles, heat pumps, industry and rapidly expanding data centres, putting growing pressure on the national grid.

Data centres, in particular, consumed 23% of Ireland's total metered electricity in 2025, scaling up from 5% in 2015. According to the Irish Central Statistics Office, total usage almost matched the electricity used by all urban and rural households combined (28%).

At the EU level, political talks are underway to agree on how to modernise the bloc's ageing power grid. More than a technicality, revamping the EU's grids is paramount for EU countries to fully utilise the vast amounts of renewable energy produced and ultimately electrify the bloc's economy.

Adding pressure to the race towards electrification, the European Commission has recently announced a 46% electrification target by 2040, in a bid to encourage EU countries to boost related investments.

A holistic approach to electrify Ireland's economy

The White Paper will examine some of the biggest questions facing the energy transition, the Irish government said. This includes how much electricity Ireland will need, where it will come from, how the grid should evolve and how the country can balance the competing priorities of affordability, security of supply and decarbonisation.

A statement from the Irish Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment said the strategy will be backed by detailed modelling of future energy scenarios, including risk assessments, demand forecasts, infrastructure needs and governance arrangements.

"This White Paper will be a key part of guiding the energy transition to clean, secure, affordable electricity. It will set a path to deliver — for this generation and future generations," O'Brien added.

"It will require national conversation and collaboration. Starting today, I invite all stakeholders across government and the public, private and voluntary sectors to work with us on this initiative."

The initiative forms part of Ireland's commitment to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 under EU law, with electrification remaining the government's central strategy for cutting emissions across transport, heating and industry.

France was the first EU country to announce its own electrification plan aimed at cutting reliance on fossil fuels. Other EU countries are likely to follow suit.

However, for the EU to fully succeed in electrifying the bloc's economy, the current high electricity prices must be addressed, or households and businesses won't have sufficient incentives to switch.

The Commission recently asked member states to ensure that electricity is not taxed more heavily than gas, while leaving governments free to determine the structure of their national tax systems under the EU's energy taxation rules.

Eva Schwab, energy poverty policy officer at the European Federation of National Organisations working with the homeless, said that electrification will only succeed if everyone is included.

Schwab regretted that the Commission plan, seen as a model for EU countries to emulate, makes no mention of energy poverty.

"Without targeted support, the households that stand to benefit most from lower energy bills will remain locked into expensive fossil fuels while better-off households capture most of the gains.”

content_html_zh:
爱尔兰宣布对其电力系统进行全面审查，政府承诺制定到 2050 年重塑该国电力行业的蓝图，以加快实现气候目标并实现经济电气化。

爱尔兰气候、能源和环境部长达拉·奥布莱恩 (Darragh O'Brien) 周三表示，正在制定一项长期战略，以制定爱尔兰到 2050 年如何发电、传输和调节电力的计划。

都柏林此举之际，爱尔兰已担任欧盟理事会轮值主席国，并誓言将电气化作为优先事项。

中东的混乱也揭示了欧盟对进口化石燃料的依赖如何导致更高的能源费用和通货膨胀，在霍尔木兹海峡中断的短短 111 天内，欧盟在化石燃料进口上额外花费了大约 500 亿欧元。

奥布莱恩表示：“爱尔兰的能源转型对我们所有人来说都是一个重大机遇，有助于提高我们的经济和工业的效率和竞争力，为企业创造新的机会，并为爱尔兰各地的社区创造切实的利益。”

随着爱尔兰从化石燃料转向电力经济，新的《电力部门白皮书》预计将成为未来能源政策的基石，指导立法、投资决策和电网发展。

此次审查之际，预计未来几十年电力需求将在电动汽车、热泵、工业和快速扩张的数据中心的推动下激增，给国家电网带来越来越大的压力。

尤其是数据中心，到 2025 年，其消耗的电力将占爱尔兰总计量电力的 23%，较 2015 年的 5% 有所增加。 根据爱尔兰中央统计局的数据，总用电量几乎相当于所有城乡家庭用电量的总和（28%）。

在欧盟层面，政治谈判正在进行，以就如何实现欧盟老化电网的现代化达成一致。 改造欧盟电网不仅仅是一个技术问题，对于欧盟国家充分利用所生产的大量可再生能源并最终实现欧盟经济电气化至关重要。

欧盟委员会最近宣布到2040年电气化率达到46%的目标，以鼓励欧盟国家加大相关投资，这给电气化竞赛增添了压力。

爱尔兰经济电气化的整体方法

爱尔兰政府表示，白皮书将探讨能源转型面临的一些最大问题。 这包括爱尔兰将需要多少电力、电力从哪里来、电网应如何发展以及该国如何平衡负担能力、供应安全和脱碳等相互竞争的优先事项。

爱尔兰气候、能源和环境部的一份声明表示，该战略将得到未来能源情景详细模型的支持，包括风险评估、需求预测、基础设施需求和治理安排。

“本白皮书将成为指导能源向清洁、安全、负担得起的电力转型的关键部分。 它将为这一代人和子孙后代开辟一条实现目标的道路，”奥布莱恩补充道。

“这需要全国性的对话和合作。 从今天开始，我邀请政府、公共、私营和志愿部门的所有利益相关者与我们合作实施这一举措。”

该倡议是爱尔兰根据欧盟法律到 2050 年实现气候中和的承诺的一部分，而电气化仍然是政府减少交通、供暖和工业排放的核心战略。

法国是第一个宣布自己的电气化计划的欧盟国家，旨在减少对化石燃料的依赖。 其他欧盟国家可能也会效仿。

然而，欧盟要想在欧盟经济电气化方面取得全面成功，就必须解决当前的高电价问题，否则家庭和企业将没有足够的动力进行转换。

欧盟委员会最近要求成员国确保电力税收不高于天然气税收，同时让各国政府根据欧盟能源税收规则自由决定其国家税收体系的结构。

欧洲国家组织联合会与无家可归者合作的能源贫困政策官员伊娃·施瓦布表示，只有所有人都参与进来，电气化才会成功。

施瓦布感到遗憾的是，被视为欧盟国家效仿典范的欧盟委员会计划并未提及能源贫困问题。

“如果没有有针对性的支持，那些从降低能源费用中受益最多的家庭将继续使用昂贵的化石燃料，而富裕家庭则获得大部分收益。”
